purpose: Machine-independent referent for census claims over a MIXED tree — part git-tracked API output, part locally regenerable crop bulk, part ignored runtime residue. Claims 006-output-dir-standard#32[1] and #34[1] anchor to this manifest, not to the directory (Obs 383: the same walk returns 48,707 on amd-tower and 127,281 on sapphire).
composition_note: This is NOT a wholly regenerable tree. Its 1,538 tracked files are API-derived proposer/verifier outputs that cost money to recreate and are already in git; its PNG bulk is locally regenerable from those tracked files plus untracked rasters; its logs and batch payloads are ignored runtime residue. The manifest therefore partitions the tree rather than describing a single recipe.

determinism.status: counts-deterministic; content-hashes not asserted at scale
determinism.evidence: The crop-generation path used by this project was demonstrated byte-deterministic across hosts on 2026-08-03 (see regen-manifests/gs-125m-fp-side-6-crop-review.json § determinism). That test exercised gs-fp-classify.render_crop, NOT scripts/extract_candidates.py, which produced this tree's crops. No byte-level determinism test was run over 47,137 files, so per-file sha256 values are deliberately NOT recorded here.
determinism.recorded_instead: Two filename-set digests (below) that ARE machine-independent: they were computed on both hosts on 2026-08-03 and matched exactly. A filename set is toolchain-independent in a way PNG bytes are not.

name_set_digests.definition: sha256 over the LC_ALL=C-sorted list of paths relative to outputs/h11/pv-diag-384/crops of every *.png file beneath it
sha256 over the LC_ALL=C-sorted list of paths relative to outputs/h11/pv-diag-384 of every file that is not *.png, *.log, *.jsonl or *.backup
name_set_digests.note: This set is IDENTICAL to the tracked-core set below — not merely equal in cardinality; the two path sets were compared element-wise on 2026-08-03 and neither difference is non-empty. Every non-bulk, non-runtime file in this tree is git-tracked, so the only unrecoverable content is crop PNG bulk (regenerable) plus logs and batch payloads (ignored residue).

name_set_digests.definition: sha256 over the LC_ALL=C-sorted `git ls-tree -r HEAD --format='%(objectname) %(path)'` listing for the tree
name_set_digests.note: Derived from the git index, so it is machine-independent by construction at a given commit — recorded as a cross-check on the two filesystem digests above.

generator.scope: crop PNGs and their candidate_manifest.json siblings only
generator.note: The tracked JSON/GeoJSON core of this tree is NOT produced by this script — it is proposer and verifier output from paid API runs and is recoverable from git, not by regeneration.

tracked_inputs.role: per-condition extraction recipes; each records source_geojson, padding, crop_dimensions and the candidate list. These are the machine-independent statement of what the crop bulk SHOULD contain.

untracked_inputs.note: Byte-identical on amd-tower and sapphire as at 2026-08-03. Not git-tracked (.gitignore:3, :5); bundle-index stratum under ruling 15.

parameters.source: GeoTIFF rasters preferred, tile PNG fallback (E33 fix)
parameters.note: Per-condition parameters are recorded in each of the 34 candidate_manifest.json files listed under tracked_inputs; they are not restated here to avoid a second, drift-prone copy.

census.scope_definition: The set of files present on BOTH surveyed hosts on 2026-08-03. Measured independently on each host with `find -type f` (no symlink following, per the Obs 385 census convention) and reconciled by extension; the two filename-set digests above confirm set identity, not merely equal cardinality. amd-tower's tree is exactly this common set; sapphire's is a strict superset.

host_excess_breakdown.note: All five subtrees EXIST on amd-tower; only their PNG payloads were removed there (a local disk cleanup). No tracked file differs between the hosts.

known_shortfall.description: The tracked recipes expect 51,677 crop PNGs under crops/; 47,137 are present. The 4,540-file shortfall is confined to exactly two cells and is IDENTICAL on both hosts, so it is a property of the tree, not of a machine.
known_shortfall.note: Discovered while assembling this manifest (Session 125). Both cells' candidate_manifest.json records failed_extractions = 0, so the crops were generated and later removed rather than never produced. Regenerating them would restore the tree to its recipe; no claim currently depends on them.
